<content>
1: # Component registry
2: 
3: The reuse engine. **Check here before harvesting anything.** If a page needs a
4: component that already exists, compose it and skip the Figma → UI kit → pattern
5: library round trip entirely.
6: 
7: ## Layout
8: 
9: ```text
10: components/<component-name>/
11: ├── README.md        # required: what it is, where it came from, how to install it
12: ├── *.html           # verbatim markup fragment(s) when harvested from markup
13: ├── *.css            # only if the component carries its own styles
14: ├── manifest.json    # required: source, fragments, css/js, assets, figma pointer
15: ├── verify.json      # required: section spec (counts, taps, expectCss/hoverCss/pressCss)
16: ├── figma/           # only if the component is Figma-editable (see below)
17: │   ├── spec.json    # paste source: root key, instances, props, geometry, overrides
18: │   ├── copy.json    # moved copy/icons/props (Figma is boss for copy)
19: │   ├── build.js     # one-shot rebuild (must reproduce the frame with no hand-patches)
20: │   ├── evidence/    # committed verification screenshots (final frames only)
21: │   └── README.md    # per-component edit notes (paste/edit/replace commands)
22: └── assets/ or *.svg # images/icons the fragment references
23: ```
24: 
25: `figma/` holds the Figma-editable counterpart: `spec.json` lets any agent
26: paste the component as a live instance with correct properties, edit those
27: properties, and replace a page instance — no cross-file copy/paste needed
28: (Plugin API has none). Workflow: `skills/figma-component-edit` +
29: `tooling/figma-export.js` / `figma-paste.js` / `figma-replace.js`. Every script that
30: sends code to Figma goes through **`tooling/figma-run.js`** (CLI + `callFigma(code,
31: fileKey, desc)`): one payload transport, one place where proxy noise is filtered and a
32: `Error:` line decides the exit code. Section builders live in the project
33: (`ongoing_project/<project>/figma/<section>/build.js`) and assert their own output —
34: see `ongoing_project/sage50accountant/figma/README.md`.
35: `play-overlay` is the pilot; add `figma/` to a component when its Figma
36: properties first need editing — not upfront. Cross-cutting references:
37: `docs/kit-variables.md` (all 478 kit variables with per-breakpoint values —
38: grep here before any Figma variable scan), `skills/build-instruction`
39: (instruction + term registry rules mirror these mechanics).
40: 
41: `site-header` carries **`navigation/`** instead of `figma/`. The nav is not a page
42: section — there is no pattern to paste — so its Figma side is a config-driven kit:
43: one JSON per market drives a builder that writes GN01 + SN01 into any design file as
44: live library instances, plus a gate that asserts the same config against the live
45: page DOM. Start at `site-header/navigation/README.md`; the CA worked example is
46: `ongoing_project/sage50accountant/figma/nav/` (its `build.js`/`verify-nav.js` are
47: wrappers over the kit, so there is one implementation to fix).
48: 
49: ## Term registry (`figma/terms.json`, schema v1) + builder token lint
50: 
51: No component composes without a term registry: `source` (instruction frame,
52: pattern demo, Figma section, site), `breakpoints` ([390,768,1440,1920]),
53: `terms[]` (rendering/layout: `term`, `cmsIdPrefix`, `site` class, `figma`
54: counterpart, `status`), `params[]` (sized values: `term`, `token` as
55: authored, `kitVar` {name, values} | bound-string | NONE, `figma` value,
56: `siteBreakpoints`[4], `status`, `verify`, `note`), `autoWrappers[]`
57: (renderings in saves but not instructions, mechanism + pending proof),
58: `nameMismatches[]`, `openQuestions[]`. Status enum: `match`,
59: `match-responsive`, `match-geometric`, `match-large/responsive-mid`,
60: `GAP-*`. Reference: `pn02-highlights-6col/figma/terms.json`.
61: 
62: `tooling/check-builder-tokens.js` is the authorship gate: every number a
63: `figma/build.js` payload writes must be a named const, a copy.json/spec
64: value, or a `// token-allow: <num> <reason>` entry (derivations marked
65: `Phase 4: compute`). Clean exit 0 required pre-commit (AGENTS.md gates).
66: 
67: ## New-component variable integration (instruction → Figma → Vercel)
68: 
69: Every new component ships this chain, in order — none of it optional:
70: 
71: 1. **Instruction first:** write the Sitecore tree + option tokens
72:    (`skills/build-instruction` §1), one term per rendering.
73: 2. **Registry:** `figma/terms.json` (schema v1 above) with `options[]` on
74:    every option-family param (all legal tokens + site classes + Figma
75:    values + proof) and `bindings[]` for every live binding, prop, and
76:    style link.
77: 3. **Figma build:** masters by key, layout frames (never bare FIXED),
78:    variables BOUND not written (`setBoundVariable` after import-by-KEY),
79:    text styles ASSIGNED by key on exact size match (sole genuine override
80:    kept), slots/props pinned — then `check-bindings.js` 100% green.
81:    **Rhythm included: the spacing is a bound FIELD (the frame's own
82:    `paddingTop`/`paddingBottom`, a `paddingBottom` on the heading stylebox,
83:    a bound `itemSpacing` per gap), never a `spacer` frame and never an
84:    absolute y.** A filler frame is a number nobody owns and carries one
85:    fixed value; a bound field carries the `Breakpoints` mode (40 at Mobile,
86:    80 at Large desktop) and cannot drift. Assert the token name as well as
87:    the resolved value (`boundName(node, 'paddingTop')` — a raw 80 and a
88:    bound 80 read back identically) and assert that no filler frame survives.
89:    How the same pattern is built in the reference file (`XO7YuDahwIZ1WCq8IoQ6Mo`)
90:    is the construction to copy; see `skills/figma-section-replace` and
91:    `figma/README.md` rule 6 for the CA HB05/TS03 numbers.
92: 4. **Site compose:** pattern demo verbatim, option classes only (triple
93:    proof: variant + bundle + CMS saves), zero custom values.
94: 5. **Sync proof:** `translate-variables.js --comp` clean both... dry-clean
95:    Figma→site AND a reverse report that shows the way back; write paths
96:    proven on a throwaway fixture, never on live files.
97: 6. **Gates:** token lint + bindings + sync-check green before commit.
98: 
99: ## README must record
100: 
101: | Field | Why |
102: |---|---|
103: | `source:` | `atomic-ui` \| `pattern-library` \| `custom` — atomic-ui wins (roadmap 1.5) |
104: | Source URL / snippet path | re-harvest without re-discovering |
105: | Harvested date + version/pin | detect drift |
106: | Install snippet | copy-paste into a page |
107: | Fallbacks / known gaps | JS-driven states, library drift, no-JS notes |
108: | Used in | which pages depend on it (grep this before changing it) |
109:

232: | [`ar-cb07`](ar-cb07/) | pattern-library (CB07, AR talk-to-experts copy) | `ongoing_project/cpp/vendor-payment-services` |
233: 
234: ## Terminology (binding)
235: 
236: - **Pattern** — a named Sitecore design (`HB05`, `PN11`): has a snippet path
237:   and a pattern-library page. Patterns are *harvested*, never invented.
238: - **Component** — a built, registered unit under `components/<name>/`
239:   (fragment + fallback CSS/JS + assets + README + manifest). Components are
240:   *composed* into pages. One Figma section = one component.
241: - **Element** — a nested part *inside* a component (hero eyebrow, portal table,
242:   a card). Elements live and are verified with their parent component; they are
243:   NOT separately registered.
244: - **Promote element → component only on second use.** If an element is needed
245:   by another page/section, extract it then — not before. (HB05's portal mock
246:   stays an element until something else needs it.)
247: - **Instance / Variant (Figma)** — an instance is a usage of a library
248:   component; a variant is a prop-driven version (`style: single cta`,
249:   `Colour: over dark`). Rebuilds preserve instances via import-by-key, never
250:   SVG-flatten them (`skills/figma-uikit-to-design`).
251: - **Figma spec** — `components/<name>/figma/spec.json`: the paste source for
252:   a component's live Figma instance (root key, nested instances, props,
253:   geometry, `overrides`). Edits are recorded as `overrides` so every agent
254:   and every future paste gets them (`skills/figma-component-edit`).
255: 
256: ## Rules
257: 
258: 1. A component built for a page is saved here **first** (markup + assets +
259:    README), then composed into the page. The page is the last step, not the first.
260: 2. Copy, never hand-rewrite, harvested markup — rewrite only where a documented
261:    fallback is required (see `skills/clone-web-element`).
262: 3. Figma update to an existing page: if every section maps to a registered
263:    component, edit the prototype HTML directly.
264: 4. Keep component folders dependency-free — no imports from other components
265:    unless the README says so, so a page can include just what it needs.
266: 5. Figma edits go through `figma/spec.json`, never bare `use_figma` one-offs:
267:    export → record `overrides` → paste to scratch → screenshot-verify →
268:    replace on the page (`skills/figma-component-edit`). Commit the updated
269:    spec with the change so the next agent pastes the edited version.
270: 6. After every fold into a one-shot Figma builder, re-prove it fresh and
271:    screenshot-compare before swapping; re-save the Figma baseline only for
272:    a verified intended change (never to silence a diff) and re-point all
273:    stored node ids. Rules of engagement: `skills/figma-component-edit` §4.
274: 7. Shared tree: rebase, never force-push; re-run the sync gate after every
275:    pull; stage only your own files (a parallel session works here).

(End of file - total 275 lines)

# Component registry

The reuse engine. **Check here before harvesting anything.** If a page needs a
component that already exists, compose it and skip the Figma → UI kit → pattern
library round trip entirely.

## Layout

```text
components/<component-name>/
├── README.md        # required: what it is, where it came from, how to install it
├── *.html           # verbatim markup fragment(s) when harvested from markup
├── *.css            # only if the component carries its own styles
├── manifest.json    # required: source, fragments, css/js, assets, figma pointer
├── verify.json      # required: section spec (counts, taps, expectCss/hoverCss/pressCss)
├── figma/           # only if the component is Figma-editable (see below)
│   ├── spec.json    # paste source: root key, instances, props, geometry, overrides
│   ├── copy.json    # moved copy/icons/props (Figma is boss for copy)
│   ├── build.js     # one-shot rebuild (must reproduce the frame with no hand-patches)
│   ├── evidence/    # committed verification screenshots (final frames only)
│   └── README.md    # per-component edit notes (paste/edit/replace commands)
└── assets/ or *.svg # images/icons the fragment references
```

`figma/` holds the Figma-editable counterpart: `spec.json` lets any agent
paste the component as a live instance with correct properties, edit those
properties, and replace a page instance — no cross-file copy/paste needed
(Plugin API has none). Workflow: `skills/figma-component-edit` +
`tooling/figma-export.js` / `figma-paste.js` / `figma-replace.js`. Every script that
sends code to Figma goes through **`tooling/figma-run.js`** (CLI + `callFigma(code,
fileKey, desc)`): one payload transport, one place where proxy noise is filtered and a
`Error:` line decides the exit code. Section builders live in the project
(`ongoing_project/<project>/figma/<section>/build.js`) and assert their own output —
see `ongoing_project/sage50accountant/figma/README.md`.
`play-overlay` is the pilot; add `figma/` to a component when its Figma
properties first need editing — not upfront. Cross-cutting references:
`docs/kit-variables.md` (all 478 kit variables with per-breakpoint values —
grep here before any Figma variable scan), `skills/build-instruction`
(instruction + term registry rules mirror these mechanics).

`site-header` carries **`navigation/`** instead of `figma/`. The nav is not a page
section — there is no pattern to paste — so its Figma side is a config-driven kit:
one JSON per market drives a builder that writes GN01 + SN01 into any design file as
live library instances, plus a gate that asserts the same config against the live
page DOM. Start at `site-header/navigation/README.md`; the CA worked example is
`ongoing_project/sage50accountant/figma/nav/` (its `build.js`/`verify-nav.js` are
wrappers over the kit, so there is one implementation to fix).

## Term registry (`figma/terms.json`, schema v1) + builder token lint

No component composes without a term registry: `source` (instruction frame,
pattern demo, Figma section, site), `breakpoints` ([390,768,1440,1920]),
`terms[]` (rendering/layout: `term`, `cmsIdPrefix`, `site` class, `figma`
counterpart, `status`), `params[]` (sized values: `term`, `token` as
authored, `kitVar` {name, values} | bound-string | NONE, `figma` value,
`siteBreakpoints`[4], `status`, `verify`, `note`), `autoWrappers[]`
(renderings in saves but not instructions, mechanism + pending proof),
`nameMismatches[]`, `openQuestions[]`. Status enum: `match`,
`match-responsive`, `match-geometric`, `match-large/responsive-mid`,
`GAP-*`. Reference: `pn02-highlights-6col/figma/terms.json`.

`tooling/check-builder-tokens.js` is the authorship gate: every number a
`figma/build.js` payload writes must be a named const, a copy.json/spec
value, or a `// token-allow: <num> <reason>` entry (derivations marked
`Phase 4: compute`). Clean exit 0 required pre-commit (AGENTS.md gates).

## New-component variable integration (instruction → Figma → Vercel)

Every new component ships this chain, in order — none of it optional:

1. **Instruction first:** write the Sitecore tree + option tokens
   (`skills/build-instruction` §1), one term per rendering.
2. **Registry:** `figma/terms.json` (schema v1 above) with `options[]` on
   every option-family param (all legal tokens + site classes + Figma
   values + proof) and `bindings[]` for every live binding, prop, and
   style link.
3. **Figma build:** masters by key, layout frames (never bare FIXED),
   variables BOUND not written (`setBoundVariable` after import-by-KEY),
   text styles ASSIGNED by key on exact size match (sole genuine override
   kept), slots/props pinned — then `check-bindings.js` 100% green.
   **Rhythm included: the spacing is a bound FIELD (the frame's own
   `paddingTop`/`paddingBottom`, a `paddingBottom` on the heading stylebox,
   a bound `itemSpacing` per gap), never a `spacer` frame and never an
   absolute y.** A filler frame is a number nobody owns and carries one
   fixed value; a bound field carries the `Breakpoints` mode (40 at Mobile,
   80 at Large desktop) and cannot drift. Assert the token name as well as
   the resolved value (`boundName(node, 'paddingTop')` — a raw 80 and a
   bound 80 read back identically) and assert that no filler frame survives.
   How the same pattern is built in the reference file (`XO7YuDahwIZ1WCq8IoQ6Mo`)
   is the construction to copy; see `skills/figma-section-replace` and
   `figma/README.md` rule 6 for the CA HB05/TS03 numbers.
4. **Site compose:** pattern demo verbatim, option classes only (triple
   proof: variant + bundle + CMS saves), zero custom values.
5. **Sync proof:** `translate-variables.js --comp` clean both... dry-clean
   Figma→site AND a reverse report that shows the way back; write paths
   proven on a throwaway fixture, never on live files.
6. **Gates:** token lint + bindings + sync-check green before commit.

## README must record

| Field | Why |
|---|---|
| `source:` | `atomic-ui` \| `pattern-library` \| `custom` — atomic-ui wins (roadmap 1.5) |
| Source URL / snippet path | re-harvest without re-discovering |
| Harvested date + version/pin | detect drift |
| Install snippet | copy-paste into a page |
| Fallbacks / known gaps | JS-driven states, library drift, no-JS notes |
| Used in | which pages depend on it (grep this before changing it) |

## Terminology (binding)

- **Pattern** — a named Sitecore design (`HB05`, `PN11`): has a snippet path
  and a pattern-library page. Patterns are *harvested*, never invented.
- **Component** — a built, registered unit under `components/<name>/`
  (fragment + fallback CSS/JS + assets + README + manifest). Components are
  *composed* into pages. One Figma section = one component.
- **Element** — a nested part *inside* a component (hero eyebrow, portal table,
  a card). Elements live and are verified with their parent component; they are
  NOT separately registered.
- **Promote element → component only on second use.** If an element is needed
  by another page/section, extract it then — not before. (HB05's portal mock
  stays an element until something else needs it.)
- **Instance / Variant (Figma)** — an instance is a usage of a library
  component; a variant is a prop-driven version (`style: single cta`,
  `Colour: over dark`). Rebuilds preserve instances via import-by-key, never
  SVG-flatten them (`skills/figma-uikit-to-design`).
- **Figma spec** — `components/<name>/figma/spec.json`: the paste source for
  a component's live Figma instance (root key, nested instances, props,
  geometry, `overrides`). Edits are recorded as `overrides` so every agent
  and every future paste gets them (`skills/figma-component-edit`).

## Rules

1. A component built for a page is saved here **first** (markup + assets +
   README), then composed into the page. The page is the last step, not the first.
2. Copy, never hand-rewrite, harvested markup — rewrite only where a documented
   fallback is required (see `skills/clone-web-element`).
3. Figma update to an existing page: if every section maps to a registered
   component, edit the prototype HTML directly.
4. Keep component folders dependency-free — no imports from other components
   unless the README says so, so a page can include just what it needs.
5. Figma edits go through `figma/spec.json`, never bare `use_figma` one-offs:
   export → record `overrides` → paste to scratch → screenshot-verify →
   replace on the page (`skills/figma-component-edit`). Commit the updated
   spec with the change so the next agent pastes the edited version.
6. After every fold into a one-shot Figma builder, re-prove it fresh and
   screenshot-compare before swapping; re-save the Figma baseline only for
   a verified intended change (never to silence a diff) and re-point all
   stored node ids. Rules of engagement: `skills/figma-component-edit` §4.
7. Shared tree: rebase, never force-push; re-run the sync gate after every
   pull; stage only your own files (a parallel session works here).
